points.text: Claim that attention-based methods cannot work with FlashAttention is inaccurate; block-wise probing exists.
Claim that existing methods are static is misleading; Top-p dynamic methods exist.
Only compared against StreamingLLM and H2O; baselines insufficient.
More video benchmarks needed (VideoMME, LongVideoBench, NextQA, etc.).
No evaluation on long videos exceeding 20k context.
More extensive experiments on LLaVA-Video expected.
Cross-layer estimation seems unnecessary and may compound information loss.
Method needs attention scores, appearing incompatible with FlashAttention.
Figure 1(c) could more clearly show dense vs ST-SpAttn differences.
Weak theoretical justification that lower-layer scores suffice for higher layers.
No analysis of PureKV computational overhead.
Baselines weak; add AdaKV, PyramidKV, HeadKV, PruneVID.
Writing quality could be improved.
Core techniques individually not novel.
Layer assignment for CLIE vs ST-SpAttn empirical, not principled.
Audio-visual results relegated to appendix; test on audio-capable models.
Non-monotonic budget-performance relationship not investigated.
Only single-query evaluation; multi-turn and cache reuse untested.
Early-layer attention guiding later layers resembles GemFilter/FastV; shared principle not discussed.
Value-norm and temporal redundancy close to uncited InfiniPot-V; claim about prior work contradicted.
Absolute novelty statement about sparse-attention design should be hedged.
Prior work mischaracterized; many citations wrong or unrelated.
Closest VLM KV-compression baselines (VL-Cache, MEDA, InfiniPot-V) not compared.
FastV behaves very differently across models, unexplained.
Baselines lack sparse attention; compression and sparse prefill effects confounded.
Correlation 0.2-0.4 is not sufficiency; 'prove' misused; need top-h overlap.
'Negligible degradation' claim fails on VideoLLaMA2.
Evaluation limited to MVBench; AVSD single numbers.
Reproducibility details missing (w, h, frames, layers).
No limitations section.
Metric called ROUGE in one place, accuracy in another.
Task naming inconsistent: AC duplicated, 10 columns vs 14 tasks.
Table 5 +0.0016 gain described as significantly outperforming.
Ablation 'significantly decreases' rests on one task with small differences.
Modest engineering contribution with narrow evidence; closer to workshop level for ICLR.
Typos, unreadable Fig. 5, inconsistent reference formats.
'Negligible degradation' contradicted by large VideoLLaMA2 drops.
5.0x and 3.16x headline numbers unmeasured or from sparse attention, not compression.
ROUGE used on multiple-choice benchmark; metric and parsing unclear.
Full-cache scores at or below chance on some tasks.
LOOK-M implausibly low, likely implementation failure; missing from Table 2.
Task subsets differ per model, unexplained; AC duplicated.
Single runs, no CIs; differences within noise; beating full cache suspicious.
Ablations on one task only; CLIE effect negligible.
Missing ST-SpAttn-only control at full cache.
Hyperparameter selection protocol unstated; Fig. 5 sweep on reported task; layer inconsistency.
Hyperparameters w, h, frames, prompts, decoding, batch not given.
Table 3 lacks baselines despite claim of faster than comparison methods.
Latency protocol undefined: ms/token, FlashAttention use, sparse kernel.
Short clips; KV size not bottleneck; long videos needed for efficiency claims.
App. 6.2 'significantly outperforms' with +0.0016 gain.
Suspected copy errors: identical values in Table 5 and Table 2.
Typos, reversed table reference, caption abbreviations.
Configuration selection protocol unstated; sweep on a reported task.
No ST-SpAttn-only control; eviction and sparse prefill confounded.
'Purification' asserted but never measured.
Overclaims: negligible degradation, stable, significantly outperforms.
ROUGE on multiple-choice benchmark.
Sub-chance full-cache scores and outlier values.
LOOK-M near 0.06, likely broken baseline.
Motivated by long high-resolution video but evaluated on short clips.
Unrelated and mislabelled citations.
AC duplicated in Table 2 header; table order reversed in text.
Suspected copy error: SnapKV and StreamingLLM identical in Table 5.
'Sufficient statistic' and 'prove' used for a correlation.
Motivated long-video, memory-bound deployment regime untested; settings unstated, one GPU.
Sparse mask assumptions (spatial alignment, anchor frame, fixed grid) not stress-tested.
Handling of text tokens and mask construction for Qwen2.5-VL undescribed.
Single shared ranking across layers and heads ignores heterogeneity; needs per-layer comparison.
No systems/roofline analysis explaining latency behaviour.
No limitations or broader-impact paragraph.

P.summary: Mischaracterizes prior work as static sparsity.
Weak baselines; stronger KV methods missing.
Cross-layer estimation questionable; information loss risk.
Weak theory for lower-layer score sufficiency.
Layer assignment empirically chosen, not principled.
Multi-turn and cache reuse not evaluated.

Q.summary: Citation quality and mischaracterized prior work.
No ST-SpAttn-only control; sparse prefill confound.
Evaluation limited to short MVBench clips; no long videos.
Metric unclear: ROUGE vs accuracy on multiple choice.
Efficiency evidence thin: no baseline latency, protocol undefined.
Shared ranking across layers/heads ignores heterogeneity.
